metadata.case_name: LAM CHOR MUN v. HO TIN WAH AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.education_level: Primary 6 at time of accident; resumed schooling in Form 1 in November 2002; since 2006 in Grade 9 in the United States (equivalent to Form 3)

injuries.description: Head injury including occipital bruise, generalised tonic clonic convulsion and post-concussional syndrome
source: Physical examination showed that she had a small patch of bruise over her occiput.
The Plaintiff then developed generalised tonic clonic convulsion and was later admitted into the Orthopaedic Ward of the Tuen Mun Hospital.
Dr. Yu's report commented inter alia that the Plaintiff was suffering from post-concussional syndrome ("PCS").
Dr. Woo: "As a result of the head injury, she has residual headache and absent-mindedness, consistent with the diagnosis of a very mild post-concussional syndrome."
injuries.icd_description: Concussion with loss of consciousness, duration unspecified or unknown due to lack of information

injuries.description: Abrasions over her left arm and right ankle
source: Abrasions were found over her left arm and right ankle.

injuries.description: Dirty crushing injury over her left dorsal foot with loss of skin, exposure of tendon and bones
source: She suffered dirty crushing injury over her left dorsal foot with loss of skin, exposure of tendon and bones.
injuries.icd_description: Crushing injury of other parts of foot

injuries.description: Fracture of her left distal tibia and fibula
source: Fracture of her left distal tibia and fibula

injuries.description: Compound fracture of her left 4th and 5th metatarsal bones; deformity of the 4th toe
source: compound fracture of her left 4th and 5th metatarsal bones were found.
deformity of the 4th toe on her left foot.

injuries.description: Scarring and skin graft donor site scars (including surgical scars at groins, skin donor site at left buttock, abrasion and laceration scars and skin grafted site over dorsum of foot)
injuries.body_part: right groin; left groin; left buttock; left shin; dorsum of left foot
source: the Plaintiff had the following scarring on her body: (1) 14 cm surgical scar at her right groin; (2) 17 cm surgical scar at her left groin; (3) 17 x 17 skin donor site scar at left buttock, pale and not hypertrophic; (4) 13 x 3 cm abrasion scar at left shin; (5) 4 cm laceration scar at left shin; and (6) 10 x 6 cm skin grafted site scar over dorsum of foot, hypertrophic at distal half, with local tenderness.

manifestations.description: Lost consciousness for a while after the accident
Residual pain in her left knee
Residual pain in her left foot with prolonged walking and standing
Stiffness of the toes on her left foot
Deformity of the 4th toe on her left foot
Embarrassment / reluctance to show scars; afraid of wearing sandals, shorts or short skirts; cannot wear pointed shoes
Unable to run for any long distance without feeling pain
If she continued walking or standing for 10 minutes, there would be pain to her left foot

treatments_received: Emergency operation for debridement of the wound and close reduction and internal fixation of her left distal left tibia and fibula (17 August 2002)
Second operation for debridement and reduction and fixation of the toe fractures (19 August 2002)
Third operation for wound debridement and skin grafting (26 August 2002)
Two further operations for debridement and skin grafting and removal of the implants (dates not separately specified)
Excision of the scar over the dorsum of her left foot and skin grafting taken from both groins (10 December 2004)
Debridement of the wound over her left foot (January 2005)
Physiotherapy (12 sessions from 31 October 2002 to 13 February 2003)
Pressure garment management of scar condition (from 12 November 2002 until re-admission on 10 December 2004)

losses.description: Embarrassment to show the scars and deformed toe; afraid of wearing sandals, shorts or short skirts; cannot wear pointed shoes.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Had to give up the idea of attending dancing classes and participating in the swimming gala of her school; she used to lead a more active life but was less active after the accident.
Unable to run for any long distance without feeling pain; pain if walking or standing for 10 minutes; residual pain on prolonged walking/standing.
Plaintiff's social life and leisure/sports activities were materially and adversely affected.
